subject: Nimbus: unexpected mid-cycle usage reallocation and proposed settlement
messages:
From: Alex Romero <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaSOps Team <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle usage spike / possible misattribution (invoice attached)

Jordan —

We just received the November invoice (attached) and there is a ~3.8x increase in tokens billed for our ingest pipeline between 11/14 and 11/17. We run a steady stream of ingests and these days are outliers compared to our median usage. We've attached a short CSV snapshot from our side showing request_ids and top-level paths. Can you confirm whether these were billed under our primary tenant or routed to the staging namespace?

Key asks:
- A simple explanation of what changed on your side that could cause a spike in billed tokens across the tenant boundary.
- If this is attributable to a migration/routing change on Redwood's side, we need a remediation plan and evidence for a credit.
- Please indicate next steps for a temporary hold on the invoice while this is investigated — we have monthly procurement windows.

Thanks,
Alex Romero
Billing Operations
Nimbus Analytics

Attachments: invoice_NIM-202611.pdf (PDF), usage_snapshot_20261119.csv (CSV)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage spike / possible misattribution (invoice attached)

Alex —

Thanks for flagging this and for the CSV — that was very helpful. I'm opening this thread with our billing and infra leads (cc'd). Initial notes from a quick look at our side:

- We saw a short-lived routing change in our edge router on 11/14 @ 03:00 UTC that rebalanced some prefetched requests. That window lasted ~36 hours while a rollout was healed.
- The rolling change toggled a tenant tag enrichment step in the ingestion proxy; a minority of requests lost the tenant_tag header during re-route and were billed under a fallback namespace rather than Nimbus's primary tenant.

What we'll do next (48-hour plan):
1) Export the server-side logs for the 11/14-11/17 window (request_id mapping + tenant_tag) and share a CSV proof set.
2) Run a reconciliation against the tokens counted under Nimbus's org id and the fallback namespace to compute delta.
3) Propose a one-time settlement for the confirmed misattributed tokens. Proposed settlement: one-time credit equal to 48 hours of median daily usage for Nimbus (goodwill while we improve tagging safeguards).
4) Freeze the invoice while we complete the reconciliation if procurement requires it — let us know your procurement contact and deadline.

Ben / Kim — can you pick up the logs export and token delta calc? I think finance will need the proposed credit amount and the mapping evidence (request_id pairs).

Alex, I'll follow up with the exported proof set no later than 11/21. Apologies for the disruption — we treat misattribution seriously and will add a post-mortem to the release notes.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----

> 
> We just received the November invoice (attached) and there is a ~3.8x increase in tokens billed for our ingest pipeline between 11/14 and 11/17.
> 
> Attachments: invoice_NIM-202611.pdf, usage_snapshot_20261119.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Romero <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus: unexpected mid-cycle usage reallocation and proposed settlement

Jordan / Kim —

I've pulled the logs for 11/14 02:30 UTC through 11/17 04:00 UTC. Preliminary reconciliation shows ~1,240,512 tokens attributed to the fallback namespace that have matching request_ids present in Nimbus's CSV. Breakdown:
- 78% of the misattributed tokens were from prefetched batch requests during a single autoscaler rebalancing event.
- 18% were from a scheduled config push where the enrichment container restarted and dropped tenant headers for in-flight requests.
- 4% are still under investigation (edge timeouts, retried requests).

I ran a quick cost calc against Nimbus's rate band — the misattributed amount translates to $5,960 of billed consumption. Per Jordan's suggestion, a one-time credit equal to two days of Nimbus's median daily spend (~$6,200) looks reasonable as an operational goodwill concession.

For evidence: I'll publish a CSV with the request_id pairs (fallback -> Nimbus) and a token count column, and deposit it to the shared drive link Jordan shared. Kimberley, can you confirm Finance sign-off on the $6,200 provisional credit and whether we need a JIRA to track the post-mortem?

Ben
Senior Billing Analyst
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nimbus_reconciliation_20261120.csv (will be uploaded to shared drive)

From: Alex Romero <billing@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus: unexpected mid-cycle usage reallocation and proposed settlement

Jordan / Ben / Kim —

Thanks for the rapid investigation and for the detailed evidence set Ben. I reviewed the request_id mapping and token counts; that lines up with our internal tracing. Appreciate the proposed credit — that matches our expectation for a goodwill remedy.

A couple of quick asks to close the loop:
- Please send a short joint statement we can include in our procurement ticket confirming the credit and the root cause (one paragraph).
- Confirm whether the invoice will be put on hold or if we should expect an updated invoice reflecting the credit for November's billing cycle. Procurement wants a formal invoice adjustment.

If you send the statement and a revised invoice or credit memo to billing@nimbus-analytics.com by EOD Wednesday 11/24, we'll process the adjusted payment in the next cycle.

Best,
Alex
Billing Operations
Nimbus Analytics
